title: Fifty years since the Emergency: Thengadi and the fight for democracy
author: Editorial Desk
summary: On 25–26 June 1975 civil liberties were suspended. The movement that followed drew in people from every field.
body:
On the night of **25 June 1975**, the Government of India declared an Emergency. Press censorship was imposed, thousands of political workers were detained and fundamental rights were curtailed. It remained in force until March 1977.

## The place of labour

Trade unions were among the groups affected. Their activity was restricted and many leaders were arrested. The wider anti-Emergency movement, organised through underground networks, brought together people of many political views.

## Thengadi Ji's role

BMS's own history records that **Dattopant Thengadi** organised protests as part of the anti-Emergency movement, using the organisational network of the Sangh family and his experience of public life. His belief was that a labour organisation cannot be indifferent to the survival of democracy, since the rights of workers depend on it.

## What the Emergency teaches

- Freedom of association is not a gift of the State. Where it is suspended, workers are the first to lose a voice.
- The institutions that protect rights need citizens who will defend them.
- Different groups can work together in a common cause.

Every year, 25 June is remembered in India as *Samvidhan Hatya Diwas* by a notification of the Government in 2024. Whatever one's view of it, the lesson of the period belongs in any account of Indian labour.
